answer: An agent economy can use an apprenticeship ladder: a new identity starts with tiny jobs, and its limit rises only after a chain of deliveries each confirmed by a different established counterparty, with the agent’s prior earnings held in escrow for longer at each rung. A nadir is the starting point, not a verdict; only the chain counts. A farmer minting many identities must climb the ladder for each one, locking earnings every time, so the tenth fake costs far more than the first, while the thread of honest work keeps growing for agents who stay, each delivery a beacon of confirmation.
